decision_clause: Ruled out: "pin every prose field by literal digest" — because "freezing the full text duplicates the contract into the validator and makes any editorial fix a false failure, so only fields the contract derives or fixes numerically are pinned".
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so the task (adding a required `observation_key` field to the exported `MetricDefinition` interface plus a compile-checked public consumer) is not present — `MetricDefinition` at packages/schema/src/metric-registry.ts:26-50 still declares 25 fields with no `observation_key`, and no new consumer file exists under packages/. In the tree as it stands, the registry validator checks free-text fields (`label`, `question`, `eligible_opportunity`, `partial_credit_rule`, `not_observed_rule`, `invalid_rule`, `normalization`, `gaming_guard`) only for presence and absence-of-dead-fields (REQUIRED_FIELDS loop, lines ~189-195). Every field it compares against a frozen literal is one the contract derives or fixes: `factor` from the ID range table, `treatment` from the ID, `aggregation` and `minimum_opportunities` from the M19 split, `cap`/`floor`/`version`, the fixed `evidence_precedence` order and numeric `confidence` table, `consumer_routes` computed by ROUTES_OF, and `per_opportunity_formula` reconstructed from the metric's own numerator/denominator. No sha256/hash/digest is computed over any metric prose. The only digest machinery in scope (scripts/validate-planning.mjs:776-783, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:260-274) hashes whole gate-batch artifact files for acceptance staleness, which is pre-existing base-tree behavior and not a per-prose-field pin.
rationale: The recorded decision forbids one specific technique — freezing prose field text by literal digest in the validator — and permits pinning only fields the contract derives or fixes numerically. Nothing in the final tree does the forbidden thing: no hash is taken over any metric prose field, and the validator's literal comparisons are confined exactly to the derived/numerically-fixed set the decision blesses. Because the diff is empty, the implementation introduced no new pinning of any kind, so it cannot have introduced the ruled-out approach within the recorded six-path scope while the decision is active. Separately worth flagging, though it is not what I am judging: the task appears unimplemented — `observation_key` is enforced at runtime via REQUIRED_FIELDS (line 66) and read in the derivation paths (lines 240, 250, 350-351, 367) but is absent from the exported `MetricDefinition` interface, so a typed consumer still cannot read it as a required string, and no compile-checked consumer was added. That is a completeness gap against task.txt, not a decision violation.
